title: MedFabric: Gold Evidence Hides the Difficulty of Word-Level Medical Fabrication Detection
abstract: arXiv:2605.04180v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models fabricate in medicine, producing fluent statements that are factually wrong, so reliable fabrication detection is a prerequisite for clinical deployment. Reported progress on this task is inflated by two evaluation artifacts: an authorship-style shortcut, where human-written ground truths are paired with LLM-written hallucinations so detectors key on writing style rather than facts, and the provision of gold evidence at test time. A benchmark that tests factual reasoning must therefore remove the style shortcut, ground every fabrication in a real retrievable passage, and score detectors across the range of evidence quality faced in deployment. We build MedFabric to these requirements, a benchmark of 646 word-level medical fabrications, each paired with a ground truth that shares its LLM authorship and near-identical surface form (median ROUGE-L 0.95). tldr: MedFabric通过消除风格捷径并提供与虚构内容表面形式高度相似的真实证据，揭示了词级医学虚构检测在实际部署中的真实难度。
